changelog.entry: Optional soft sound, off unless you turn it on in Settings (Sound): a quiet bell when a ship comes safely past, and a faint, slow hum under the night that has its own switch and goes quiet in a hidden tab. The sounds are made in your browser (no sound files), have a volume and a Reduce sounds switch, and nothing in the game depends on them.

Twenty-one achievements: eleven for simply keeping the light (every one reachable in a Quiet year) and ten for the story layer, six of them hidden until you solve the mystery they belong to. Earning one shows a toast, and the Achievements panel counts the two groups separately.

A guided tutorial from the opening screen, a compact status strip and pinned night controls on phones, and an About the Light panel that explains how the rules work and gives four real lighthouse facts with their sources named and the date they were read.

The light is not quite as quiet as it looks. Six small mysteries play out across the first year: a second light on the water, a chair that keeps turning, a knocking at the cistern, an extra cup, letters nobody signed, and a ferry that is not on any chart. Each one builds, looks for a moment like something worse, and then turns out to be a person, an animal or the floor. A notebook fills in as you go. Nothing frightening ever happens, and two switches are always in reach: Eerie details in the toolbar skips the odd things and keeps the letters, and Story hides the whole layer.

Passing sailors now have names. Ten people write to the keeper once their boat has got safely by often enough: a quiet mail captain, a fisher who never catches anything, a smuggler of pickled walnuts, a surveyor who corrects charts, a child on the ferry, two correspondents who write through you, and more. Letters sometimes carry a gift that appears in the keeper's room, and some letters let you choose a reply. The Letters button lists everything you have found, and the Story button hides all of it.

The first year is now a complete game: forty nights, four seasons, a year-end screen with a Copy result button, and then you may keep the light for as long as you like. Settings has Abandon this year and Reset all progress (both ask first), and a welcome-back line greets you on return.

The day now matters: five tasks of daylight to mend the station, sleep, tidy the room or walk the tideline, a workshop where salvage buys nine upgrades, and an order form for the supply boat's twelve crates. Three standing goals sit at the top of the page, with no order and no deadline, and the seasons change the weather, the ships and the length of the night.

Lighthouse is a cozy keeping game. Each evening you read the barometer and the harbour board, set the lamp for dusk, deep night and dawn, and decide how the keeper spends the night. Then the night plays out, with pause and 1x, 2x and 4x speeds, and a morning report says which ships found the light.
